## Phase 2: Agent Creation in Copilot Studio

### Step 2-1. Create a New GHCP Agent

Use Home > Agent or Agents > New agent. Set the display name to `{{AGENT_NAME}}`
exactly, without adding GHCP. Verify the harness and Agent settings before the
first save. Reuse this name when selecting the published agent in a workflow.

### Step 2-2. Add Knowledge and Tools

Configure approved sources through Build > Knowledge. Distinguish connector
ingestion from runtime retrieval; indexed ServiceNow articles are retrieved via
M365 search/semantic index, not a direct agent connection to ServiceNow.
For agent-called operations, use Build > Tools and verify actual actions and
authentication. Implement scenario-defined contracts during setup. Operations
called by the surrounding workflow are not automatically agent tools.

### Step 2-3. Update Agent Instructions

```text
You are {{AGENT_NAME}}.
{{COMPLETE_GLOBAL_SCOPE_GROUNDING_PRIVACY_LANGUAGE_ENTRY_PATH_AND_FAILURE_RULES}}
```

### Step 2-4. Add Runtime Skills

Import every skill included in the standard configuration. Use Build > Skills >
Add skill > Upload a skill for each standalone SKILL.md in
[matrix order](0.Resources/Skills/README.md). Package supporting assets with
SKILL.md in a ZIP if needed. Alternatively Create from blank or Generate with AI,
then inspect names, descriptions, instructions and actual dependencies.

### Step 2-5. Add Suggested Prompts

{{SOURCE_STYLE_TITLE_PROMPT_TABLE}}

### Step 2-6. Configure Requested Workflow Entry

Include this step only when event-driven behavior is requested. Configure the
verified event trigger in Workflows, add **Agent > An existing agent**, select
the published `{{AGENT_NAME}}`, pass trusted context through **Message**, and
validate the returned result before the deterministic action. Cite current
Workflows and connector guidance. Verify actual harness support and identity.

Document recipient/source access, policy authorization, duplicate prevention,
status and exception handling in the matrix. Do not require per-message human
approval for authorized routine autonomous events unless the approved policy
requires it. Configuration and go-live requirements do not make this an optional
extension. A genuinely unsupported invocation must be named as a setup blocker.

---

## Phase 3: Testing

### Step 3-1. Test Interactive Behavior

Use Preview for matching, non-matching and composed requests. Inspect available
execution details. Use Evaluate with the intended version and test identity;
verify exact acceptance criteria in addition to any AI quality score.

### Step 3-2. Test Additional Capability Flows

{{POSITIVE_BOUNDARY_COMPOSED_AND_FAILURE_CASES_FOR_EACH_CAPABILITY}}

Keep operator-paused, denied, empty, unavailable, partial, failed, pending and
unknown outcomes distinct. For writes test exact-payload authorization, any
required approval, concurrency and reconciliation.
Use isolated/non-sending tests before an explicitly approved action pilot. Record
real results separately from expectations in [Sample prompts](4.Sample-prompts.md).

---

## Phase 4: Deployment to {{APPROVED_CHANNELS}}

### Step 4-1. Publish and Pilot

{{CURRENT_HOST_SPECIFIC_PUBLISH_STEPS_AND_OFFICIAL_LINKS}}

### Step 4-2. Monitor and Roll Back

{{OWNERSHIP_QUALITY_SOURCE_HEALTH_COST_AND_ROLLBACK}}

Publish only after relevant acceptance and approval. Preserve shared connections
used by enabled capabilities; coordinate maintenance/rollback pauses with tools,
backends and stale sessions. Isolated mock tests precede a restricted action pilot;
release authorization is not an extra per-message approval requirement.
